title: Directing a project: the five board activities
blurb: Name the five directing a project activities, what triggers each one and what the board decides in it.
question: The project manager has assembled the PID and asked for authority to deliver the project. Which directing a project activity responds?

teach.body: Formally: directing a project has five activities: authorize initiation, authorize the project, give ongoing direction, authorize a stage or exception plan, and authorize project closure. In plain English: four of them are formal yes-or-no decisions in answer to a request from the project manager; the fifth is the board's continuing advice and response to problems.

teach.body: The board reviews and approves the project brief and the initiation stage plan and confirms that investing in initiation is worthwhile. It can decide with or without a formal meeting, as long as all members agree and the project manager receives a documented instruction from the executive to proceed. A verbal nod alone is not enough.

teach.body: At Riverside Academy Trust, project manager Mei Tanaka requests initiation for a new sports hall. The board agrees by email and executive Colin Rourke sends Mei a written instruction to proceed. Later the board approves the PID in authorize the project. At each stage end it reviews the stage and approves the next stage plan, and Mei is informed. Finally it authorizes closure, checks the post-project benefits reviews and notifies the trust's business layer.

teach.text: Classic traps: the board REQUESTS an exception plan in give ongoing direction but APPROVES it in authorize a stage or exception plan. A next stage plan is approved at the end of every stage EXCEPT the final one. A stage starts only when the board says so. The project manager is informed of, not consulted on, the stage decision.

items: Five activities: authorize initiation; authorize the project; give ongoing direction; authorize a stage or exception plan; authorize project closure.
Four answer PM requests from SU, IP, SB and CP; give ongoing direction runs throughout.
Authorize initiation can be done without a meeting if all agree and the executive gives documented instruction.
Authorize closure: confirm closure, make sure post-project benefits reviews cover operational use, notify the business layer.

summary: You can now name the five directing a project activities, match each to its trigger and output, and recall what the board does in each, including the RACI rows for ongoing direction and stage authorization.

A.q: Which directing a project activity responds to the request to initiate from starting up a project?
options: Authorize a stage or exception plan
A.why: Authorize initiation responds to the request to initiate: the board reviews the brief and initiation stage plan and decides whether initiation is worthwhile (14.4.1).

whyNot.0: Authorize the project responds later, to the request for project authorization at the end of initiation.
whyNot.2: Give ongoing direction covers advice and exceptions during the project, not the formal start of initiation.
whyNot.3: Authorize a stage or exception plan responds to requests from managing a stage boundary.

A.q: In which activity does the project board approve the project initiation documentation?
A.why: In authorize the project the board approves the PID, including the management approaches and project plan, and confirms a viable business case (14.4.2).

whyNot.0: Authorize initiation approves the brief and initiation stage plan; the PID does not exist yet.
whyNot.1: Give ongoing direction provides advice and responds to exceptions; it is not where the PID is approved.
whyNot.2: Authorize project closure confirms the project can close; the PID was approved much earlier, at the end of initiation.

A.q: Which directing a project activity lets board members give informal guidance or answer requests for advice at any time?
options: Authorize a stage or exception plan
A.why: Give ongoing direction lets the board, or individual members, offer guidance and respond to requests for advice at any time (14.4.3).

whyNot.1: Authorize a stage or exception plan is a formal decision at a stage end or after an exception.
whyNot.2: Authorize the project is a one-off decision at the end of initiation.
whyNot.3: Authorize initiation is a one-off decision at the end of starting up a project.

B.q:
Which two statements about the 'authorize initiation' activity are correct?
1. The board approves the full business case and the project plan.
2. Its output is the project authorization notice.
3. It can be done without a formal meeting if all members agree and the executive gives documented instruction.
4. The board reviews and approves the project brief and the initiation stage plan.
B.why: Authorize initiation can be done without a formal meeting under those conditions (3), and the board reviews and approves the brief and initiation stage plan (4) (14.4.1).

whyNot.0: Both are false: the full business case and project plan come from initiation, and the output here is the initiation notice.
whyNot.1: Statement 1 is false: the full business case and project plan are approved when the project is authorized.
whyNot.2: Statement 2 is false: the project authorization notice comes from authorize the project; this activity issues an initiation notice.

B.q: Identify the missing words in the following sentence. In the 'authorize a stage or exception plan' activity, the [?] should be informed of the decision rather than consulted.
B.why: The RACI table shows the project manager as informed in authorize a stage or exception plan (14.6, tab 14.2).

whyNot.1: The senior user is consulted in this activity.
whyNot.2: Project assurance is consulted in this activity.
whyNot.3: The executive is accountable and responsible for this activity.

B.q: In 'authorize project closure', what should the board make sure the post-project benefits reviews cover?
options: The team managers' use of work packages
The accuracy of the original mandate
How the product performs in operational use
The number of issues raised in each stage
B.why: The board makes sure the post-project benefits reviews cover the project product's performance in operational use, including any beneficial or adverse side-effects (14.4.5).

whyNot.0: Work package performance is reviewed during the project, not in post-project benefits reviews.
whyNot.1: Benefits reviews look at what the product achieves in use, not the original mandate.
whyNot.3: Issue counts belong to project evaluation and lessons, not benefits reviews.

C.q: An exception report reaches the board. Which activity handles it, and in which activity would a resulting exception plan be approved?
options: Authorize the project; give ongoing direction
Give ongoing direction; authorize project closure
Give ongoing direction; authorize a stage or exception plan
Authorize a stage or exception plan; authorize the project
C.why: The board responds to exception reports in give ongoing direction, where it may request an exception plan; it then approves the plan in authorize a stage or exception plan.

whyNot.0: Authorize the project is the decision at the end of initiation, not the response to an exception report.
whyNot.1: The first part is right, but an exception plan is approved in authorize a stage or exception plan, not at closure.
whyNot.3: The exception report is handled in give ongoing direction; authorize the project is not used for exception plans.

C.q: In the 'give ongoing direction' activity, which board role is responsible for user-related direction?
C.why: The RACI table shows the senior user as responsible for user-related direction in give ongoing direction (14.6, tab 14.2).

whyNot.0: The executive directs on business matters; user-related direction is the senior user's responsibility.
whyNot.2: The senior supplier represents supplier interests, not users.
whyNot.3: Project assurance is consulted in give ongoing direction, not responsible.

C.q: Which practice is applied in directing a project when the board validates highlight reports and end stage reports?
C.why: Tab 14.3 lists assuring fair progress reporting, by validating highlight and end stage reports and approving exception reports, under the progress practice.

whyNot.0: Quality is applied by approving the PPD and the quality management approach.
whyNot.1: Risk is applied by approving the risk management approach.
whyNot.2: Business case is applied by approving the benefits management approach.

reteach.title: Requests in, authorizations out
reteach.question: How can you match every formal board activity to the process that asks for it?

blocks.h: Four requests, four answers, plus advice
blocks.body: Each managing-level process that ends with a request has a matching board activity. Starting up asks to initiate; the board authorizes initiation. Initiating asks for authorization; the board authorizes the project. A stage boundary asks for the next stage or an exception plan; the board authorizes it. Closing asks to close; the board authorizes closure. Ongoing direction fills the gaps.

From
Board activity
rows: Request next stage or exception plan
Authorize a stage or exception plan

blocks.text: Give ongoing direction has no single trigger: it runs throughout, answering advice requests and exception reports.

explain.body: Review and approve the project brief and initiation stage plan, and confirm initiation is worth the investment. It can be done without a formal meeting if all members agree and the PM gets documented instruction from the executive. Output: the initiation notice.

test.q: What must the project manager receive if the board authorizes initiation without a formal meeting?
options: Verbal agreement from the senior user
An initiation notice from team managers
A signed PID from the business layer
test.why: Without a formal meeting, all members must agree and the PM must receive documented instruction from the executive to proceed (14.4.1).

whyNot.1: Verbal agreement from one member is not documented instruction from the executive.
whyNot.2: Team managers do not issue board decisions.
whyNot.3: The PID does not exist until initiation, and the business layer does not authorize initiation.

explain.body: Decide whether to proceed with the rest of the project: confirm an adequate business case shows a viable project, approve the PID including the management approaches and project plan, review the benefits management approach and issue the project authorization notice.

test.q: Which statement describes the aim of the 'authorize the project' activity?
options: Decide whether initiation is a worthwhile investment
Decide whether to proceed with the rest of the project
Decide whether the final stage can be closed early
Decide which team manager will deliver each product
test.why: Authorize the project decides whether to proceed with the rest of the project, based on the PID and full business case (14.4.2).

whyNot.0: Whether initiation is worth investing in is decided in authorize initiation.
whyNot.2: Premature closure is a different decision, not the aim of authorizing the project.
whyNot.3: Allocating work to team managers is done by the PM through work packages.

explain.body: Informal guidance and answers to requests for advice at any time, from the board together or individual members; responses to exception reports, perhaps asking for an exception plan; and responses to advice from the business layer.

test.q: Who can give ongoing direction to the project manager?
options: Team managers acting on behalf of the board
Project support acting on the executive's behalf
The whole board or individual board members
The business layer for each work package
test.why: Ongoing direction can come from the board collectively or from individual members (14.4.3).

whyNot.0: Team managers take direction from the PM; they do not direct on the board's behalf.
whyNot.1: Project support provides administration to the PM and has no directing role.
whyNot.3: The business layer advises the board; it does not direct individual work packages.

explain.body: A stage starts only when the board says so: it reviews the current stage and approves the next stage plan at the end of every stage except the last, or approves an exception plan. At the end it authorizes closure, checks post-project benefits reviews and notifies the business layer.

test.q: At the end of which stages does the board approve a next stage plan?
options: Every stage including the final one
The initiation stage and no others
Stages that have had an exception
Every stage except the final one
test.why: The board authorizes the next stage at the end of every stage except the last, because the final stage ends with closure (14.4.4).

whyNot.0: There is no next stage after the final stage, so no stage plan is approved then.
whyNot.1: Every stage except the final one is followed by a stage authorization, not the initiation stage alone.
whyNot.2: After an exception the board approves an exception plan; next stage plans are approved at normal stage ends.
